stem.text: Evaluate the improper integral \( \int_{3}^{\infty} \frac{9 x^{2}}{\left(x^{3} + 5\right)^{2}}\,dx \), or show that it diverges.

worked_solution.text: The integral is improper because the upper limit of integration is infinite, so write it as \( \lim_{R\to\infty} \int_{3}^{R} \frac{9 x^{2}}{\left(x^{3} + 5\right)^{2}}\,dx \).
Substitute \( u = x^{3} + 5,\ du = 3 x^{2}\,dx \). The limits become \( u = 32 \text{ to } u = R^{3} + 5 \), and an antiderivative in u is \( - \frac{3}{u} \).
Evaluate the limit: \( \lim_{R\to\infty} \left( - \frac{3}{R^{3} + 5} + \frac{3}{32} \right) = \frac{3}{32} \). The limit is finite, so the integral converges to \( \frac{3}{32} \).

options.label: The integral converges to \( 3 \).
options.derivation: the original x limits kept after the substitution and the factor 1/3 dropped as well

options.label: The integral converges to \( \frac{9}{32} \).
options.derivation: the factor 1/3 that du introduces dropped

options.label: The integral converges to \( 1 \).
options.derivation: the original x limits kept after the substitution, the u antiderivative evaluated from u = 3 to infinity
